assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology from the incretin effect to receptor agonists that transformed diabetes and obesity care is a rare complete arc from physiological discovery to a major therapy, with large demonstrated benefit and now cardiovascular and renal outcome data. Importance, originality and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst established GLP-1 biology in humans, Drucker defined its intestinotropic and physiological actions and pharmacology, and Knudsen led the development of long-acting analogues. Mojsov and others (e.g., Habener, not credited here) made peptide-characterisation contributions, so the three-person cap forces a difficult exclusion.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and enormous clinical uptake. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Knudsen, Mojsov and uncredited early contributors is contested.
Exact historical priority claims for GLP-1 sequence and activity are from memory and not verified here.
Whether the committee views the prize as basic physiology or drug development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has reshaped circuit analysis, including the dissection of motor and locomotor circuits. The originality, clarity and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth and Boyden turned them into neuronal tools; Miesenboeck contributed an earlier genetic photoactivation concept. The three-laureate cap leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, so the configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: widely replicated for 15+ years, with clinical translation emerging (retinal restoration) but not essential to the case.
uncertainties: Several equally credible subsets of the six credited names exist.
Relative weight of discovery of the channelrhodopsin versus its neuronal deployment is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signalling principle and a fundamental proteostasis mechanism, with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell biology. Conceptually clean and highly original.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter identified the Ire1/HAC1/Hac1 and UPR pathway in yeast and mammals. Credit is compact, though other groups (e.g., Ron, Kaufman, Shen) contributed on mammalian branches and are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: mechanisms confirmed across species for roughly three decades, and prior major awards support the stability of the interpretation.
uncertainties: Contributions of mammalian PERK/ATF6 branch discoverers are not captured by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living therapeutics with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; impact on medicine is large and still expanding to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed clinically effective CAR designs and trials; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Other contributors (e.g., Eshhar, Kalos, Brentjens) are outside the credited names, so credit is spread.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: multiple approved products and years of follow-up, though long-term safety and solid-tumour efficacy remain open.
uncertainties: Attribution is diffuse across several teams.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and toxicity.
Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed the treatment of Parkinson's disease and is a landmark of translational neurophysiology that also opened circuit-based therapy for other disorders. From a motor-systems view, its importance is clear and well documented.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's 1987 observation that high-frequency thalamic stimulation suppresses tremor, followed by subthalamic targeting, is the decisive contribution; subthalamic circuit knowledge (DeLong, others) was essential but those names are not credited, which weakens a single-laureate configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of randomised trials and hundreds of thousands of implants; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Single-laureate credit omits foundational basal ganglia circuit contributors.
Mechanism of action of DBS remains incompletely understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a lethal childhood disease into a treatable one and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a platform. Mechanistic clarity and clinical impact are strong.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ASO targeting of SMN2; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and clinical development. This pairing is coherent, although Ionis/Biogen teams and SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up, though the field is still young relative to the longest-standing prizes.
uncertainties: SMN gene discovery credit is separate and not included.
Long-term durability data continue to accrue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the central cellular model of synaptic plasticity and learning, with deep influence on neuroscience. Its link to behavioural memory is still debated but the physiological discovery is foundational.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo discovered LTP in 1973; Collingridge defined NMDA receptor dependence. Morris linked NMDA-dependent plasticity to spatial learning behaviour and is a strong alternative to Collingridge.
assessment.maturity: Mature after 50 years, though causal equivalence between LTP and memory remains partly unresolved.
uncertainties: Choice of third laureate between Collingridge and Morris is unclear.
Whether LTP is sufficient to explain memory storage is still contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signalling is a central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing with broad relevance to cancer, ageing, immunosuppression and metabolism. Importance and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and defined its role in growth control; Schreiber's work on the FKBP12-rapamycin complex and mTOR target identification was important, as was Sabatini's mTORC1 nutrient-sensing work. Credit among these is open and partly overlapping with Heitman and Sabatini contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic science with rapalog use in transplantation and oncology, though disease-modifying translation in ageing is unproven.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and others not credited is unresolved.
Sabatini's inclusion may raise non-scientific concerns that I cannot verify here.
